title: DropBack: real Sandbox price protection, buyer to merchant
_actions: The automated runner drives these same UI targets through a real PayPal Sandbox checkout and live Channel3 price check.
_clips: PayPal approval is captured by the automated buyer runner. Email and password fields are masked in the recorded approval clip.

scenes.narration: A buyer chooses the Sony headphones from Holloway Goods, with fourteen days of DropBack price protection.
The storefront creates a real PayPal Sandbox order for the selected product and sends the buyer to PayPal checkout.

scenes.on_screen: PayPal Sandbox buyer login and payment approval
scenes.narration: The automated Sandbox buyer signs in and approves the payment. PayPal captures the order before DropBack opens the buyer portal.

scenes.on_screen: Scenario replay · Day 3 · live Channel3 offer
scenes.narration: In an accelerated third-day scenario, the buyer asks Channel3 to check the exact model against current in-stock offers.

scenes.on_screen: Buyer requests the verified price difference
scenes.narration: Channel3 finds a lower price. The buyer submits the live evidence and asks for the verified difference instead of returning the item.

scenes.on_screen: Merchant review · AG Grid case queue and AI report
scenes.narration: The merchant reviews the buyer note, verified market offer, return probability, return costs, and a clearly drafted message in AG Grid.

scenes.on_screen: Merchant approval · PayPal Payments v2 refund
scenes.narration: After merchant approval, DropBack sends the difference to the buyer through PayPal Payments v2 with a request idempotency key.

scenes.on_screen: APIMatic PayPal API contracts · Orders v2 and Payments v2
scenes.narration: APIMatic's PayPal context manifest documents the API contracts used for the real sandbox order, capture, and refund calls.
